source_text: Nunc ergo redeamus ad tabernaculum ecclesiae Dei vivi. Vasa sanctorum non mutis animalibus sed rationabilibus hominibus in humeris portanda sunt; duriora mutis imponuntur. Merari quattuor plaustra, Gerson duo: durioribus operibus plures quasi animalia inserviunt; ad rationabilia pauci accedunt. Ad mystica solis sacerdotibus patentia nec animalis homo nec eruditi nondum sacerdotales accedunt — per speculum et in aenigmate, operta in humeris portant, actu magis quam revelatione. Digni efficiamur ordine sacerdotii, ne irrationabilibus onera gravia imponantur. Genus regale sacerdotium sumus; acceptam gratiam vitae meritis adaequemus, ut discedentes adsumamur inter sacerdotes Dei, revelata facie gloriam Domini speculemur, et ingrediamur terram sanctam per Dominum Iesum Christum, cui gloria in saecula. Amen.
pass_a_gloss: Now therefore let-us-return to tabernacle of-church of-God living. Vessels of-holy-things not by-mute animals but by-rational humans on shoulders to-be-carried are; harder-things on-mutes are-placed. Merari four wagons, Gershon two: to-harder works more as-if animals serve; to rational-things few approach. To mystic-things to-only priests open neither animal man nor learned not-yet priestly approach — through mirror and in riddle, covered-things on shoulders they-carry, by-act more than by-revelation. Worthy let-us-be-made of-order of-priesthood, lest on-irrational heavy burdens be-placed. Race royal priesthood we-are; received grace by-of-life merits let-us-match, that departing we-may-be-taken among priests of-God, with-unveiled face glory of-Lord we-may-behold, and we-may-enter land holy through Lord Jesus Christ, to-whom glory unto ages. Amen.
pass_b_english: Now let us return to this tabernacle of the [[church of the living God >> Bible:1 Timothy 3:15]]. The vessels of the holy things should be borne on the shoulders of rational people, not mute beasts; the harder loads are laid on the mute. Merari receives four wagons, Gershon two: more serve the cruder works as if animals; few approach the rational tasks. To the mystic things open only to priests neither the [[natural man >> Bible:1 Corinthians 2:14]] nor the merely learned who have not yet risen to priestly grace may come — they see [[through a mirror, in a riddle >> Bible:1 Corinthians 13:12]], carry what is veiled on their shoulders, and know more by deed than by unveiled knowledge. Let us be made worthy of the priestly order, lest heavy burdens be laid on us as on the irrational. We are a [[royal priesthood >> Bible:1 Peter 2:9]]; let us match received grace with the merits of life, that when we depart we may be taken among God’s priests, [[with unveiled face behold the Lord’s glory >> Bible:2 Corinthians 3:18]], and enter the holy land through our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever. Amen.
